name: Spaghetti western
summary: A western shot in Spain and Italy on a wide 2.35:1 frame. A face fills the screen in an extreme close-up of the eyes, then the frame opens to a vast desert. Time stretches, the cut is slow, and the score is a part of the scene.

philosophy.core_thesis: An extreme close-up and an extreme wide shot, with a long wait between them, make a duel into a ritual and the land into a stage.
design_principles: Shoot in Techniscope at 2.35:1 with a 2-perf frame and shoot in colour on a hot, dry location.
Cut between an extreme close-up of the eyes (a 75mm to 150mm lens) and an extreme wide shot (a 20mm to 28mm lens).
Hold the build to a duel for 30 to 90 s before the first shot is fired.
Use a stylised, sparse set with sun, dust, stubble and sweat on every face.
Light with hard sun at a high angle, and keep the faces in deep, dark eye shadow.
Dub the sound after the shoot: loud boots, spurs, wind, one shot and a long silence.
Write the score first for the key scenes, and let the music set the length of the take.
anti_patterns: A hero in a clean white hat
A soft, polite long-shot only coverage
A moral speech before the fight

composition.framing: A 2.35:1 frame with a split: a face at the edge and a far figure at the other edge, or one eye strip that fills the full width.
composition.staging_in_depth: 2 to 4 planes: a foreground edge or a gun, a face or a body, and a far figure on the horizon.
composition.subject_placement: Faces at the edge and the horizon at 1/3 from the bottom; the centre stays empty.

principles.rule: Cut from an eye strip to a lone figure on the horizon.
principles.value: eyes 100% of frame height, figure 5% to 10%

principles.rule: Fill the wide frame with an eye strip, and place two duellists at the opposite edges.
principles.value: 2 subjects at 5% and 95% of the frame width

principles.rule: Stage a duel in depth with a foreground object, a face and a far figure.
principles.value: 3 planes, 1 close object at 10% of the frame

principles.rule: Slow the cut to a crawl before a shot, and then break it with a fast burst of close-ups.
principles.value: 30 to 90 s build, then 0.5 to 1 s cuts

principles.rule: Leave the sky and the ground empty so that the figures stand alone.

camera_and_movement.movement: A slow zoom or a dolly into the eyes; a crane that rises to reveal the town; short static wide shots.
camera_and_movement.support: Dolly, crane and tripod; a zoom lens for the push-in
camera_and_movement.camera_height: 1.0 to 1.7 m; low angle for the gunmen
camera_and_movement.move_speed: Zoom over 5 to 15 s; dolly 0.2 to 0.5 m/s

lens_and_format.focal_length: 20mm to 28mm for the wide shot; 75mm to 150mm for the eye close-up
lens_and_format.aperture: f/8 to f/11 in hard sun
lens_and_format.focus: Deep focus in the wide, a shallow focus of 0.1 to 0.3 m on the eyes

light.quality: Hard desert sun, high contrast and burned skin; in the town a low lamp or a fire.
light.direction: From the top at 60° to 80°, so the eyes sit in shadow under the hat.
light.source: Sun, reflectors and a low fire or lamp at night

colour_and_grade.treatment: A warm, dry colour print with a dust-yellow base and a deep brown shadow.
grade_recipe: Set the white balance at 5600K and push the highlights 300K warmer.
Lift the midtone saturation by 10% to 15% in the yellow and orange range.
Add a contrast curve of +25% with the black point at 4%.
Add grain at 20% to 25% and a vignette of 15%.
Keep the blue in the sky desaturated by 20%.
colour_and_grade.texture: 35mm grain at 20% to 25%, with dust and heat shimmer

editing_and_rhythm.average_shot_length: 5 to 8 s outside a duel, 0.5 to 2 s in a duel (estimate)
editing_and_rhythm.shot_length_range: 0.3 s for an eye flash to 60 s for a long build
editing_and_rhythm.cutting_logic: Cut to the music; hold the build to a duel with a rising count of close-ups, then fire and cut out.
editing_and_rhythm.transitions: Hard cut, a slow dissolve for the time of a ride and a snap cut on a shot.

sound.approach: Post-synchronised sound with a loud, simple mix: spurs, wind, flies and a creak.
sound.dialogue: Sparse and dry; the actors speak in several languages and the voices are dubbed.
sound.music: A score with a whistle, a guitar, a choir and a bell, written to lead the scene.
sound.loudness: −23 LUFS integrated, with a wide dynamic range for the silence

titles_and_graphics.treatment: A stylised title over a painted or an animated sequence; the credits in a bold western face.
titles_and_graphics.type: A heavy slab-serif in warm white or orange, 3 to 5 s per card.

shot_primer.opening: Open on a wide shot of an empty street or a far figure, hold it for 8 s, then cut to an eye strip.

canonical_works.work: The Good, the Bad and the Ugly
Once Upon a Time in the West

emotion.target_response: Tension and awe: the viewer waits inside a long silence and sees the land as a myth.

use_cases: music video with a desert setting
avoid_when: The brief needs a fast, modern action cut.
The setting is a clean, indoor or urban place without a link to the myth.

modifiers.how: Keep the stylised duel; cut to 1 to 2 s per shot, add wire work and a camera that moves in the fight.
Keep the wide frame; move to real locations, dull colour and a hero without a myth.

average_shot_length.note: A duel cuts at 0.5 to 2 s.

sources.title: Christopher Frayling, Spaghetti Westerns: Cowboys and Europeans from Karl May to Sergio Leone (Routledge, 1981)
Christopher Frayling, Sergio Leone: Something to Do with Death (Faber and Faber, 2000)
